0.name: Coccidiosis
0.description: A parasitic infection of the intestinal tract caused by Eimeria protozoa, leading to gut lining damage, bloody diarrhea, and weight loss.
treatment: Administer Anticoccidial medication (e.g., Amprolium, Sulfadimethoxine) in drinking water immediately.
Keep litter dry and clean; replace wet bedding.
Provide electrolyte and vitamin supplements (A and K) to assist gut recovery.

1.name: Healthy
1.description: No symptoms of infection detected. Bird appears healthy with normal droppings and vital parameters.
symptoms: Bright, alert eyes and active behavior
Firm, well-formed droppings with white urate caps
treatment: Continue standard feeding, fresh clean water, and vaccination schedule.
Ensure proper ventilation and dry litter management.

2.name: Newcastle Disease (NCD)
2.description: A highly contagious viral infection affecting respiratory, nervous, and digestive systems in poultry. Can cause severe flock mortality.
symptoms: Nervous signs: twisted neck (torticollis), paralysis, tremors
Sudden drop in egg production with misshapen eggs
treatment: Quarantine affected birds immediately to protect the rest of the flock.
Report suspected outbreak to official veterinary authorities.
Provide supportive care with vitamins and antibiotics to prevent secondary bacterial infections.
Strictly vaccinate uninfected birds against NCD according to local protocol.

3.name: Salmonella Infection
3.description: Bacterial infection caused by Salmonella species (e.g., S. pullorum / S. gallinarum) causing systemic illness, enteritis, and high mortality in young chicks.
symptoms: Yellowish, chalky, or white watery diarrhea (pasting of vent)
Loss of appetite and stunted growth
treatment: Administer vet-prescribed antimicrobial therapy (e.g., Enrofloxacin, Amoxicillin, or Trimethoprim-Sulfa).
Sanitize all feeding and watering equipment thoroughly.
Dispose of infected carcasses and contaminated bedding safely.
Implement rodent and pest control to prevent reinfection.
